reconstructed_words.reasoning: ἔχθρα regularly renders אֵיבָה (cf. Num 35:21-22; Ezek 25:15), and τίθημι is the standard equivalent of שׁית. Word order and syntax match MT exactly.
ἀνὰ μέσον is the stereotypical LXX rendering of בֵּין, attested hundreds of times. The 2ms suffix matches MT.
Standard equivalence γυνή = אִשָּׁה with definite article reflecting הָ-. Conjunction and syntax match MT.

reconstructed_words.lxx_word: καὶ ἀνὰ μέσον τοῦ σπέρματός σου
reconstructed_words.reasoning: σπέρμα is the standard rendering of זֶרַע throughout the Pentateuch. Suffix and conjunction match MT.

reconstructed_words.lxx_word: καὶ ἀνὰ μέσον τοῦ σπέρματος αὐτῆς
reconstructed_words.reasoning: Direct rendering with 3fs suffix = זַרְעָהּ. Matches MT exactly.

αὐτός as nominative pronoun reflects emphatic הוּא. The masculine pronoun matches MT (referring grammatically to σπέρμα/זֶרַע); LXX preserves masculine even though σπέρμα is neuter, indicating fidelity to the Hebrew masculine antecedent.

alternatives.note: Vulgate ipsa suggests feminine, but LXX clearly read הוא

reconstructed_words.reasoning: The rare verb שׁוּף poses a translation problem; the translator rendered both occurrences with τηρέω ('watch for, lie in wait against'), apparently associating שׁוּף with שׁאף ('pant after, lie in wait,' cf. Ps 56:2-3) or interpreting contextually. κεφαλή = רֹאשׁ is standard. The Vorlage almost certainly = MT; divergence is interpretive, not textual.

alternatives.note: Translator may have read or associated with שׁאף, but unlikely a different Vorlage

reconstructed_words.reasoning: πτέρνα consistently renders עָקֵב (cf. Gen 25:26; 49:17). αὐτοῦ reflects the 3ms suffix on the verb. Same translation strategy with τηρέω for שׁוּף applied consistently.

summary_technical: The reconstructed Vorlage matches MT throughout with no evidence of textual variation. The notable feature is interpretive rather than text-critical: the translator rendered the rare verb שׁוּף with τηρέω ('lie in wait for') in both clauses, likely by association with שׁאף or by contextual guess, eliminating the parallelism with κεφαλή/πτέρνα that the Hebrew preserves. No DSS evidence survives for this verse to test variants.
summary_plain: The Greek translator was working from a Hebrew text essentially identical to the Masoretic Text. The only puzzle is how he rendered a rare Hebrew verb meaning 'crush' or 'strike' as 'lie in wait for.'

bibcrit_assessment.title: LXX Genesis 3:15 reflects proto-MT Vorlage
bibcrit_assessment.reasoning: Every retrovertible element corresponds to MT; the Greek shows no textual divergence, only interpretive ambiguity around שׁוּף. The double τηρήσει is a translator's solution to an opaque verb, not evidence of a different Hebrew reading (such as שׁאף). The famous αὐτός (vs. Vulgate ipsa) confirms a masculine Hebrew pronoun הוּא agreeing with זֶרַע, exactly as MT reads.
bibcrit_assessment.plain: The Greek translator had a Hebrew text matching the traditional one. Differences in meaning come from how he handled a rare Hebrew word, not from a different source text.
